new_statements.rule_in_words: Yarshater says stress is predictable (and grammatically functional) but gives no single rule; the transcription convention and the accented examples show the default is stress on the last syllable of the word/stem, with a closed set of unstressed grammatical suffixes: the feminine marker -a, the direct/oblique and plural endings -e/-a, and the verbal prefixes be-/mi-. Nouns with the unstressed feminine -a are stressed on the stem-final (surface penultimate) syllable (déta, asífa, galína); nouns whose final -á/-ā is itself the stem keep final stress (xondāná, xā). Present-tense personal endings are stressed (p. 462); in the preterite/imperfect stress falls on the last syllable of the stem and the prefix is unstressed (p. 463); the perfect adds a stressed -e; the Gandomabadi imperfect suffix -ay is unstressed while the perfect stresses it (p. 464). This is the Persian-type pattern: final stress except for unstressed inflectional suffixes, with morphological conditioning in the verb.
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed suffixes: feminine -a, sg. obl./pl. dir. -e (p. 457), imperfect -ay in Gandomabadi (p. 464); unstressed prefixes be-/mi-; stressed present endings and perfect -e; fn. 39 p. 466: 'The stress was marked only where confusion was possible' (implying stress is otherwise predictable). Stress described as 'functional' (contrastive, e.g. stressed vs unstressed final -a).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; sketch of Hazār-rudi (Hazarrud village, Upper Tarom, Zanjan) with notes on Siāvarudi, Nowkiāni, Gandomābādi, Kalāsari, Jamālābādi, Bākoluri, Čarazai and Jeyshābādi; based on one informant (Seyfollāh Faghāni, 1965). The general stress statement (p. 454) is about Hazār-rudi.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes Hazār-rudi (village of Hazarrud, Upper Tarom, Zanjan province), the dialect Yarshater chose as representative of the Tati dialects of Ṭārom, with notes on Siāvarudi, Nowkiāni, Gandomābādi, Kalāsari, Jamālābādi, Bākoluri, Čarazai and Jeyshābādi. Glottolog uppe1235 (ISO tov Upper Taromi) has no dialect-level glottocodes; Stilo 1981 places Hazar-rud and Siavarud in Group Four A = Upper Tarom, so the source matches uppe1235. Note that Glottolog's kore1279 (Karanic) also lists Hezarrudi and Nowkiani as dialect names; those are Khalkhal (Koresh-e Rostam) villages of the same names, not the Tarom ones.

sources.locator: §3 Phonemes, p. 454 with footnote 7; supporting statements §4 p. 455, §8 p. 457, §22 p. 462, §23 p. 463, fn. 39 p. 466
sources.note: Phonemes §3 p. 454: 'The stress is functional and predictable', fn. 7: final a or e assumed unstressed unless marked; p. 455 feminine -a unstressed with accent on the preceding (stem-final) syllable (déta, béza, asífa, xeyláka, galína, xondāná); p. 457 case/plural endings -a/-e unstressed; p. 462 present personal endings all stressed; p. 463 preterite prefix be- unstressed and 'The stress is placed on the last syllable of the stem', perfect has a stressed -e; fn. 39 p. 466 stress marked only where confusion possible. No explicit general rule beyond the transcription convention.
